html:
Shooting of unarmed civil rights marchers by British paratroopers in the Bogside area of Derry, Northern Ireland, on 30 January 1972. Thirteen people died that day and a fourteenth later.

The march protested against internment, the policy of jailing suspects without trial. Soldiers of the Parachute Regiment fired on the crowd and said they had been shot at. Witnesses and later inquiries disagreed. The first inquiry, led by Lord Widgery in 1972, largely cleared the soldiers and was widely seen as a whitewash.

The Saville Inquiry, which sat from 1998 and reported in 2010, found the shootings unjustified and that none of the dead had been armed. Prime Minister David Cameron apologised.

In 1972, the killings drove many young Catholics to the Provisional IRA. In March the British government shut down the Northern Ireland parliament and ruled directly from London. It is among the defining moments of the-troubles.
sum: Shooting of unarmed civil rights marchers by British paratroopers in the Bogside area of Derry, Northern Ireland, on 30 January 1972. Thirteen people died that day and a fourteenth later.
